misc.text: 💡[Lost in Translation] Gaban’s techniques have numbers in their names. In Japanese version, the technique he uses here is “8000,” while the one he used against Luffy and Zoro was “80.” Since 80 is exactly 1% of 8000, maybe Oda is suggesting that Gaban only showed 1% of his power when he fought Luffy and Zoro.😍💪 There may also be a reason why Oda chose 80 and 8000 instead of numbers like 50 and 7000. In old Japanese expressions, numbers such as 80 and 8000 can mean a very large number, not just the exact number itself. For example, “8000 generations; Yachi” appears in Japan’s national anthem and means a very long period of time. Japan also has the old expression “8 million gods,” which does not literally mean exactly eight million gods. It means that there are countless gods.🤔 So the numbers in Gaban’s techniques may have a traditional Japanese meaning as well as the clear connection between 80 and 8000.🌏

misc.text: #ONEPIECE1190 Mojr isn't wrong. People act as if Kaido or Big Mom are a tier above Rayleigh or Gaban, but they overlook two facts: in terms of portrayal, Garp placed Rayleigh on the same level as Whitebeard. Teach, who had no qualms about fighting Law (the one who defeated Big Mom), preferred not to tangle with Rayleigh. Rayleigh's portrayal speaks for itself. Then there’s the fact that Kaido almost lost to Oden. And let's be honest: in my eyes, Oden isn't stronger than Rayleigh or Gaban. If an Oden who was already weakened could inflict such a wound on Kaido, I shudder to think what would happen if a "Divine Gate" actually hit him. It’s not a fight where one side completely destroys the other. Kaido, Big Mom, Rayleigh, and Gaban are all on the same level. It makes sense for the Pirate King's "Wings" to be on the same tier as the Yonko. It would be a extrem either way battle between these four(Kaido,Big Mom, Gaban or Rayleigh)...
